2027 BMW M 1000 RR to Get Lighter and Thinner M Motorsport Frame
9 photos
Photo: BMW Motorrad
The last time we heard anything about the BMW M 1000 RR superbike was back in September, when the German bike maker announced pricing for the limited edition Isle of Man TT. Specced in a way that honors one of the most dangerous motorcycle races in the world, it is only to be produced in 115 units, so not exactly enough of them to go around. Today’s M 1000 RR story is, however, something else entirely.
As you’re reading this, BMW Motorrad is getting ready to launch into the world the third generation of the M 1000 RR. In a move we’re not really used to, the company announced this week the initial details of the two-wheeler, or, more specifically, some details about the frame that will hold it together.
BMW chose to do this because there are plenty of changes to discuss, all of them adopted from lessons learned by the Bavarians in international racing. Everything you’re about to read in the lines below is what every new 2027 M 1000 RR will be fitted with as standard right off the factory floor.
The skeleton of the superbike will continue to be made from aluminum, but, through methods that have not been fully disclosed, BMW cut its weight down by 2.8 pounds (1.3 kg) compared to the existing version. That may not seem like much, but in the world of two-wheeled motorsport, it can mean the difference between losing and winning, as it increases agility and allows rapid changes in direction.
One of the ways BMW cut weight was by adopting thinner walls for the frame. No less than 30 percent of the wall thickness has been removed, and that also contributes to the increased flexibility. BMW says that at lean, the upcoming M 1000 RR will be able to flex laterally to a defined (and unspecified) degree, aiding the suspension system in absorbing inputs from the road surface. Despite this, the frame remains stiff enough to respond properly to braking and drive forces.
BMW did not specifically say when the new M 1000 RR will be presented in full, but don’t blame me if I hope we’ll get to see more of it during the upcoming Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show in Milan, Italy, in early November. autoevolution will be on scene for the event to bring you word on all the hottest bikes to be presented there.
Until the new superbike gets here, I’ll remind you that the current version offers a WSBK-trialed-and-tested ShiftCam engine that develops 205 hp. In this configuration, the motorcycle sells at the time of writing on the U.S. market for $35,395. The interesting part is that BMW lists this version as being a 2027 model year...
